incident_description: A production PostgreSQL service exhausted its connection pool after a deployment left connections open, causing request timeouts and database connection errors.
root_cause: Application connections were not returned to the pool on an exception path.
fix_applied: Closed connections in a finally block, added pool exhaustion metrics, and restarted affected workers.

incident_description: A MySQL-backed API became unavailable when a traffic increase consumed every available database connection and new requests stalled.
root_cause: The connection pool limit was lower than the service concurrency and queries held connections too long.
fix_applied: Reduced query duration, corrected pool sizing, and added connection wait alerts.

incident_description: A Redis cache outage caused elevated latency because clients retried failed connections aggressively and exhausted application worker threads.
root_cause: Unbounded retry behavior amplified a short Redis availability failure.
fix_applied: Added exponential backoff with jitter, bounded retries, and a circuit breaker.

incident_description: A service returned database timeout errors after a schema migration introduced a table lock during peak traffic.
root_cause: A blocking migration ran without an online migration strategy.
fix_applied: Rolled back the migration, used an online alter procedure, and scheduled schema changes away from peak traffic.

incident_description: A Java web service gradually consumed all heap memory and was eventually killed by the container runtime.
root_cause: An in-memory request cache had no eviction policy and retained objects indefinitely.
fix_applied: Added bounded cache eviction, heap dashboards, and a load test covering cache growth.

incident_description: A Python worker fleet experienced increasing memory usage after processing large files and eventually restarted repeatedly.
root_cause: Buffered file contents were retained by a task-level collection after each job completed.
fix_applied: Streamed files instead of buffering them and cleared task references after processing.

incident_description: A Node.js API hit out-of-memory errors while handling a large batch export endpoint.
root_cause: The endpoint built the complete export in memory rather than streaming rows to the client.
fix_applied: Changed the response to a streaming pipeline and enforced export size limits.

incident_description: A containerized service began restarting after a release because memory usage exceeded its Kubernetes limit.
root_cause: The container limit was copied from a smaller environment and did not match production workload needs.
fix_applied: Adjusted resource requests and limits, then added memory utilization alerts.

incident_description: A deployment passed CI but production pods failed readiness checks immediately after rollout.
root_cause: A required environment variable was renamed in the application but not in the deployment manifest.
fix_applied: Updated the manifest, validated required settings at startup, and added deployment configuration tests.

incident_description: A web application served a blank page after deployment because the frontend assets were published under the wrong base path.
root_cause: The production build base URL differed from the path configured by the reverse proxy.
fix_applied: Aligned the Vite base configuration with the deployment path and added a smoke test for static assets.

incident_description: A Kubernetes rollout left old and new versions serving inconsistent behavior during a production release.
root_cause: The readiness probe reported healthy before the new application had loaded its dependencies.
fix_applied: Implemented a dependency-aware readiness check and paused rollout until it passed.

incident_description: A production release failed because a configuration file was omitted from the container image even though local tests passed.
root_cause: The build context excluded the file through an overly broad ignore pattern.
fix_applied: Corrected the build context, added image-content checks, and rebuilt the release.

incident_description: An API started returning HTTP 429 responses during a traffic burst from many application workers.
root_cause: Each worker maintained an independent request counter instead of sharing rate-limit state.
fix_applied: Centralized rate limiting in Redis and added client-side backoff.

incident_description: A scheduled data synchronization job was throttled by a vendor API and accumulated a growing backlog.
root_cause: The job ignored the vendor's rate-limit headers and retried immediately after failures.
fix_applied: Honored retry-after responses, added token-bucket throttling, and reduced concurrency.

incident_description: A public API integration began failing with rate-limit errors after a feature increased duplicate requests.
root_cause: The application did not cache identical lookup requests and made one remote call per frontend component.
fix_applied: Added request coalescing and a short-lived cache for identical lookups.

incident_description: A payment workflow returned errors because a third-party provider changed its response format.
root_cause: The integration assumed a field was always a string and did not validate provider responses.
fix_applied: Added schema validation, tolerant parsing, and contract tests against provider fixtures.

incident_description: An email notification service timed out when its external provider experienced elevated latency.
root_cause: Outbound requests had no timeout and occupied worker threads while waiting indefinitely.
fix_applied: Set explicit connect and read timeouts, moved notifications to a queue, and added fallback handling.

incident_description: An application received HTTP 401 responses from an external API immediately after credential rotation.
root_cause: One production deployment still used the previous secret because its secret reference was not refreshed.
fix_applied: Restarted the stale workers, corrected secret rollout automation, and added credential health checks.

incident_description: A shipping integration produced duplicate orders after a network timeout caused the client to retry a successful request.
root_cause: The remote operation was not protected by an idempotency key.
fix_applied: Added idempotency keys, persisted request state, and reconciled duplicate records.

incident_description: A search service returned intermittent 503 responses after a deploy changed the endpoint hostname.
root_cause: The new hostname was not resolvable from the production network due to missing private DNS configuration.
fix_applied: Corrected DNS configuration, added startup connectivity checks, and documented the network dependency.
